descriptionChirho: The active Qal verb meaning to bake bread or other food by means of an oven or fire, used across all finite conjugations (perfect, imperfect, imperative, consecutive).
The Nifal (passive) stem indicating that something is baked or shall be baked, with the food item as the grammatical subject rather than the person doing the baking.

The Qal participle used substantively as an agent noun denoting a professional baker, including masculine singular, masculine plural, and feminine plural forms with various prepositions and pronominal suffixes.
